coverage.main: Read all ten pages of arXiv 1911.10891v2 (12 April 2020): Sections 1-5, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-6 and references; and the ten-page CVPR 2020 open-access version. All 212 three-decimal values match between versions.
coverage.supplement: No appendix is included; a separate CVPR supplement was not retrieved or referenced in the text.
coverage.excluded_results: Diagonal (seen-classifier) cells of Table 3, Table 4 (attacks on ResNet110 variants as the seen classifier), Figure 3 (seen-classifier success after filtering), Figure 4 (detectability), Table 5 (NIMA image quality) and Figure 6 (randomness on seen R50) are not cross-model transfer outcomes.

result_groups.locator: Section 4 Datasets and Performance measures (p. 5); Table 3 off-diagonal cells
result_groups.population: P-Places365 (60 classes x 50 = 3,000 images), the whole CIFAR-10 test set (10,000) and ImageNet validation (3 random images x 1,000 classes); seven attacks crafted on ResNet50, ResNet18 or AlexNet and tested on the other two
result_groups.outcome: success rate: 'the ratio between the number of adversarial images that mislead the classifier on its most-likely predicted class and the total number of images' (prediction change relative to the classifier's clean prediction)
result_groups.evidence: The denominator is explicitly the total number of images, so neither clean-misclassified images nor seen-classifier failures are removed. The outcome is change from the classifier's own clean prediction rather than ground-truth misclassification, as for rank 28.

f1.evidence: Clean accuracy of all three classifiers on each dataset is printed with the success rates.

f2.evidence: The success rate is divided by the total number of images.

f3.evidence: Transfer success uses the same all-image denominator, with no selection by success on the seen classifier.

f4.evidence: With 3,000 or 10,000 images, a three-decimal proportion corresponds to about 3 or 10 possible counts, so counts are not uniquely recoverable.

f5.evidence: ColorFool and SemanticAdv are explicitly unrestricted color perturbations with no Lp radius; DeepFool and SparseFool are minimum-norm attacks; the BIM/TI-BIM epsilon is not stated. The proposed method's results explicitly have no norm budget.

f6.evidence: The official repository releases ColorFool generation and segmentation code but no transfer-evaluation script, classifier checkpoints or the sampled image lists. P-Places365 is a private challenge subset.

artifact_checks.result: Linked in the paper. Listed via the GitHub API (54 files, head 12 October 2020): Adversarial/ColorFool.py, misc_functions.py, script.sh, Segmentation/ (ADE20K semantic masks). No transfer evaluation or dataset lists. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Clean accuracy on the same image set is printed, but the outcome counts changes from each classifier's clean prediction rather than ground-truth errors, so the misclassification bound cannot be applied without recomputation.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Coded consistently with rank 28 (prediction-change outcome with an explicit all-image denominator).
